A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Syre work despite the revised title and formatting. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments and neural-network evaluations, including classification, VAE reconstruction, self-supervised learning, and continual reinforcement learning.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds transformer evaluations, computational-cost measurements, mode-connectivity experiments, and NTK/gradient-rank analyses.

M1.justification: Equations (6)–(7) retain the static random parameter bias, weight decay, and optional diagonal reweighting. Section 5.4 still specifies using zero diagonal-weight variance in experiments. The additional evaluations introduce no new Syre component.

E1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds CIFAR-10 evaluation under varying input-signal scales; v1 used CIFAR-10 for standard ResNet training and conducted the analogous input-rescaling sweep on MNIST. The original datasets and application tasks remain. Changing to ViT alone does not constitute new task coverage.

E2.justification: Figures 12–13 newly evaluate the sigma-asymmetric comparator from Lim et al. alongside W-asymmetric networks. W-asymmetric matches the earlier W-fix approach rather than introducing a wholly new comparator. Existing comparisons remain, and relabeling several vanilla curves as wd clarifies their existing weight decay.

E3.justification: New protocols include ViT parameter sweeps with 512-example rank measurements, resource profiling at three batch sizes, interpolation between trained MLPs, and beginning/end NTK measurements using 1,500 MNIST examples. Figure 5 also drops its earlier alpha-squared covariance-scaling specification; this reporting change does not establish that the retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices B.5–B.7 and C substantially extend the analyses: transformer sensitivity to weight decay and input scaling, computational overhead, interpolation loss barriers, and empirical NTK/gradient-rank bounds. The earlier noise-sensitivity and representation-spectrum analyses remain.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains standard deviations over ten trials, and the PPO comparison retains five-seed averaging. The new timing entries and interpolation plots include uncertainty displays, but no new run counts, estimator definitions, or statistical-testing procedures are documented; these displays accompany added results.

E6.justification: Figures 12–14 add transformer accuracy/rank results, interpolation accuracy/loss curves, and NTK/gradient-rank findings. Tables 2–3 add timing and memory measurements; for example, batch-128 ViT and Syre-ViT take 39 ± 1 and 47 ± 2 ms respectively. Original Table 1 scores and the retained plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, three propositions, five theorems, and Appendix A proofs retain their mathematical substance. Appendix C instantiates the existing propositions as a 1280 − 20n rank ceiling for an empirical check rather than introducing a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies the empirical claim from improving training to symmetry removal correlating with improved optimization or performance, and extends its capacity discussion to inference. The three principal contributions and the conclusion's central symmetry-removal claim remain.

C2.justification: The additions interpret transformer gains through rotation-symmetry removal and mode connectivity through permutation-symmetry removal. Appendix B.6 newly characterizes computational overhead as negligible. Existing qualifications about overfitting and symmetry explaining only part of the self-supervised representation gap remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds an implementation-location footnote, identifies an A6000 GPU for resource measurements, describes asymmetric-baseline hyperparameter selection, and specifies the NTK subnetwork dimensions. These improve technical disclosure, although the new experiments still lack comprehensive reproduction settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning low-rank attention, ViT implementation, symmetry/noise equilibrium, and hierarchical learning, while removing the singular-learning-theory connection. Section 3 also qualifies Lim et al.'s restriction as the scope of its proof. The main research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, selected explanations, and baseline terminology receive limited edits, and citations switch to author–year form. New appendix subsections organize the added material, but the main section sequence and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: The ICLR template changes typography, margins, headers, and figure sizing throughout. The VAE and permuted-MNIST displays move from the main text to appendix Figures 9–11. Figures 12–14 and Tables 2–3 are added, and several existing legends change from vanilla to wd.

improvement.justification: The added transformer comparisons, mode-connectivity tests, and NTK checks strengthen empirical support, while the implementation link and resource tables improve practical transparency. These gains are limited by incomplete documentation of the new experiments and an overbroad negligible-overhead interpretation: Table 2 reports 39 versus 47 ms for batch-128 ViT and Syre-ViT. The core method, theory, and earlier evidence remain substantially unchanged.
